text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تُحِلُّوا۟ شَعَٰٓئِرَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا ٱلشَّهْرَ ٱلْحَرَامَ وَلَا ٱلْهَدْىَ وَلَا ٱلْقَلَٰٓئِدَ وَلَآ ءَآمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًۭا مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَٰنًۭا ۚ وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَٱصْطَادُوا۟ ۚ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ أَن صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ أَن تَعْتَدُوا۟ ۘ وَتَعَاوَنُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلْبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ

words.gloss_range: vocative summons that opens direct legal address
words.prose: The particle {{ar:يَٰٓ}} ({{tr:yā}}) stands independently before the bridge word that follows, gathering the believers into direct address before the prohibitions begin. Its force is not semantic ornament; it makes the whole ayah a command heard by the addressed community.

topics.headline: direct summons into obligation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah begin as a summons to accountable addressees, not as detached legal description.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows consistently identify a vocative opening and command frame; QAC marks the word as a vocative particle before the address formula.

words.gloss_range: attention-bridging vocative form linking the call to the definite addressee class
words.prose: The form {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ayyuhā}}) bridges the opening call to the defined group that follows. It heightens attention before the dense legal list, keeps the relative clause within the address rather than as a separate description, and continues the legal speech-register rather than restarting it.

topics.headline: vocative bridge into the relative clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the address formula keeps the following identity clause inside the summons.
topics.reason: The rows focus on the bridge-and-alert function, and QAC identifies the ayyu-plus-hā address bundle before the relative pronoun.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun defining the addressed class within the vocative formula
words.prose: With {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}), the call becomes a defined address to those characterized by the following faith clause. The later commands are therefore tied to the believer formula instead of floating as general ritual notes.

topics.headline: believer class defined by relative link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the commands attach to a covenantal identity already named in the address.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows and QAC grammar both treat the word as the relative pronoun in apposition to the vocative address.

words.gloss_range: completed believer identity grounding the command audience; trust and security pressure remains within the faith sense
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, belief, and making secure; here Form IV marks those already characterized by faith
words.prose: The perfect verb {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) defines the addressees before any ban is issued. The root’s security and trust field gives the identity moral texture, while the local formula selects the believers as the command-bearing audience.

topics.headline: faith identity before legal duty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that obligation is addressed to an already marked community of faith and trust, not to a hypothetical future group.
topics.reason: The local perfect relative clause grounds the audience; root-pressure rows are preserved as narrowed because they enrich faith without replacing the believer-address function.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negation governing the first jussive ban and setting the refrain for later restraints
words.prose: The first {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive, not merely descriptive negation. It launches an immediate second-person ban grounded in divine legal authority rather than communal convention, then spreads through the sacred-object list and later returns as a wider rhythm of restraint.

topics.headline: first prohibition starts the cascade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah move immediately from address into binding restraint.
topics.reason: QAC marks a negative particle with jussive force, and the CRITICAL rows emphasize the initial prohibition and later repeated restraint pattern.

words.gloss_range: causative making-lawful or dissolving of protected status, forbidden in the sacred-object frame
words.root_gloss_range: untying, release, becoming lawful, alighting, and dissolving a restriction; here Form IV targets causing a protected thing to be treated as lawful
words.prose: The verb {{ar:تُحِلُّوا۟}} ({{tr:tuḥillū}}) makes the opening prohibition active: the addressees must not cause sacred things to become treated as lawful or common. The same root later marks legitimate release, but this Form IV frame targets wrongful human unbinding.

topics.headline: do not actively dissolve sanctity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ban is against producing permission or unbinding sanctity by human action.
topics.reason: Form IV causative grammar and the object list support the making-lawful/dissolving reading; broader release senses are kept as local contrast, not free replacement.

words.gloss_range: public sacred signs or rites belonging to God, with perceptible-marking pressure from the root
words.root_gloss_range: perceiving, marking, feeling, and making something noticeable; here the plural denotes recognizable ritual signs
words.prose: The plural {{ar:شَعَٰٓئِرَ}} ({{tr:shaʿāʾira}}) names the broad class of God-linked ritual signs before the ayah lists specific instances. Its root pressure makes the rites feel publicly recognizable, while local usage keeps the sense within sacred pilgrimage vocabulary, including the honoring of such signs tied to heart-guarding (22:32).

topics.headline: God-linked ritual signs as a class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first object as a class of perceptible sacred markers, not as a vague religious abstraction.
topics.reason: The construct with the divine name and plural object grammar support sacred signs; root and cross-reference rows are preserved as narrowed ritual-sign pressure.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name anchoring the rites as God’s, not communal custom
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field with disputed derivations but stable proper-name reference here
words.prose: The genitive {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) makes the preceding signs God’s signs. That relation blocks treating them as neutral custom or humanly reclassified property.

topics.headline: divine ownership of the rites
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the protected signs derive their status from relation to God.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as genitive in construct with the ritual signs, matching the CRITICAL focus on divine ownership.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle extending the prohibition to the next protected item
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) carries the force of the opening ban forward to the sacred month. It begins the list expansion that accumulates protected categories under one legal restraint.

topics.headline: conjunction extends the same ban
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the sacred month enter the same legal scope as the ritual signs.
topics.reason: The rows and QAC grammar agree that the conjunction coordinates the next object under the governing prohibition.

words.gloss_range: elliptic prohibitive negation renewing the ban before another sacred object
words.prose: The renewed {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) does not restart the sentence from zero; it repeats the prohibitive force without restating the verb. The sacred month is therefore independently foregrounded within the shared ban, carrying the sanctity concern from the prior consecration setting (5:1) into protected time.

topics.headline: renewed negative refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears each listed object receive its own prohibitive weight.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify ellipsis and repeated negation; QAC marks another negative particle continuing the prohibition chain.

words.gloss_range: the known sacred month as a visible calendar unit under the prohibition
words.root_gloss_range: visibility, public notice, and month reckoning; here the noun denotes a known sacred time unit
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلشَّهْرَ}} ({{tr:al-shahra}}) brings sacred time into the protected inventory. Its visibility field supports the sense of a publicly recognized calendar marker, while the local object slot keeps the focus on the known sacred month.

topics.headline: protected public time
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sanctity covers publicly recognized time, not only objects or places.
topics.reason: QAC gives a definite accusative object, and the CRITICAL rows connect the month to public visibility and sacred-month governance.

words.gloss_range: sacred and forbidden-to-violate quality modifying the month
words.root_gloss_range: forbidding, consecrating, inviolability, and protected precinct/status; here it qualifies sacred time
words.prose: The adjective {{ar:ٱلْحَرَامَ}} ({{tr:al-ḥarāma}}) defines the month by inviolability. The root’s sacred-and-forbidden range is active locally as protected time, part of the ayah’s larger time, House, and mosque sanctity network.

topics.headline: inviolable time
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees holiness framed through access restriction: the month is a protected zone in time.
topics.reason: Adjectival agreement with the month is local; broader precinct pressure survives as narrowed image because the word marks a protected temporal domain.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle extending the same prohibition to the offering
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the legal enumeration moving. It adds the next object under the same prohibition rather than letting the offering stand as an aside.

topics.headline: third item added with equal force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the offering enter the list with equal grammatical weight.
topics.reason: QAC and CRITICAL rows both identify coordination under the continuing ban.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negation carrying the unstated governing verb onto the offering
words.prose: This {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) gives the offering its own place in the negative cascade. The governing verb remains understood, so the object is protected without syntactic ambiguity.

topics.headline: ellipsis protects the offering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the offering protected by a repeated ban even when the verb is not repeated.
topics.reason: The row directly identifies prohibitive ellipsis, and QAC marks the word as the negative particle in the chain.

words.gloss_range: concrete sacrificial offering directed to the sanctuary; guided-gift pressure remains local
words.root_gloss_range: guiding, leading, gifting, and presenting; here the concrete noun denotes the dedicated offering animal
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْهَدْىَ}} ({{tr:al-hadya}}) names the concrete offering under the ban. Its root lets the animal be heard as a guided gift led toward its sacred destination, while the local nominal form selects the sacrificial-offering object rather than abstract guidance.

topics.headline: guided sacrificial offering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the animal as a directed, dedicated offering, not mere meat or property.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a concrete accusative noun; CRITICAL root rows are preserved as narrowed because guidance/gift pressure explains the offering without changing its local referent.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle extending the ban to garlanded consecration markers
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the offering sequence under the same legal force. It prepares the move from the animal offering to visible consecration tokens within the larger accumulation from abstract signs to time, material markers, and finally human pilgrims.

topics.headline: coordination adds marked offerings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the list move from offerings to visible markers of consecration.
topics.reason: The rows identify continued coordination in the prohibition cascade, matching QAC’s conjunction tag.

words.gloss_range: negative particle marking another protected object in the ellipsis chain
words.prose: This {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) renews the prohibition before the garlands. The repeated negation gives the visible consecration markers their own protected slot.

topics.headline: independent protection for garlands
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the garlands as independently protected, not merely implied by the offering.
topics.reason: The single CRITICAL row and QAC grammar both place this negative particle in the repeated object chain.

words.gloss_range: garlands or neck-markers that visibly signal consecrated status
words.root_gloss_range: neck-binding, garlanding, keys, and later imitation through attachment; here the plural selects visible consecration garlands
words.prose: The plural {{ar:ٱلْقَلَٰٓئِدَ}} ({{tr:al-qalāʾida}}) names the garlands as visible tokens of consecration that can mark an animal with protected status. The root’s attachment and neck-binding field supports the local image, while other branches such as keys (39:63; 42:12) remain background rather than active local senses.

topics.headline: visible consecration tokens
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a visible marker can transfer legal status to an animal in the sacred system.
topics.reason: The local object is a plural concrete marker in the ban; V4-style branch separation narrows broader root branches while preserving the marker payoff.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle that moves the prohibition from sacred objects to protected pilgrims
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) marks the decisive shift from protected objects to people heading for the House. The cascade widens from abstract signs and material markers to human pilgrims with stated motives.

topics.headline: shift from objects to people
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the list reach its climax by extending protection from things to living persons.
topics.reason: The rows emphasize the pivot to human subjects, and QAC identifies coordination extending the prohibition to the active participle.

words.gloss_range: negative particle explicitly extending the ban to the pilgrim group
words.prose: The final opening-cascade {{ar:لَآ}} ({{tr:lā}}) makes the protection of pilgrims explicit. It keeps the human target under the same prohibitive force as the sacred signs and offerings.

topics.headline: final negative in the opening cascade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears that violating pilgrims is not left as an inference from earlier sacred objects.
topics.reason: QAC and the CRITICAL row both mark this as the negative particle before the protected pilgrim group.

words.gloss_range: active participle for those heading toward or intending the Sacred House, protected while en route
words.root_gloss_range: aiming toward a center, intending, leading, origin, community, and imamate; here the participle selects directional intent
words.prose: The active participle {{ar:ءَآمِّينَ}} ({{tr:āmmīna}}) protects people while they are heading toward the House. The root’s center-orientation field sharpens their identity as a moving group aimed at a sacred destination, while broader mother, community, and leader branches remain lexical background.

topics.headline: people defined by sacred intent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the protected people are defined by their direction and intention, not by tribal label.
topics.reason: The local participle governs the House as destination; CRITICAL rows about wider root family are narrowed to directional-center pressure.

words.gloss_range: the definite House as the pilgrim destination, carrying shelter and return resonance
words.root_gloss_range: spending the night, dwelling, house, shelter, and return; here it denotes the Sacred House destination
words.prose: The definite noun {{ar:ٱلْبَيْتَ}} ({{tr:al-bayta}}) gives the pilgrims a concrete destination. Its dwelling and shelter resonance enriches the House as a place of return, while the following modifier identifies the local referent as the Sacred House.

topics.headline: specific sacred destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pilgrim intention anchored in a specific destination rather than generic piety.
topics.reason: QAC marks it as the object of the active participle; CRITICAL rows support both specific destination and cautious shelter resonance.

words.gloss_range: sacred/inviolable modifier of the House within the protected pilgrim clause
words.root_gloss_range: forbidding, consecrating, inviolability, and protected status; here it qualifies the House as protected destination
words.prose: The adjective {{ar:ٱلْحَرَامَ}} ({{tr:al-ḥarāma}}) makes the House an inviolable destination within the pilgrim-intender clause, so the movement toward it is protected together with the place itself before the pilgrims’ motives are stated. It is the middle member of the ayah’s repeated sanctity marking across time, House, and mosque.

topics.headline: the House as inviolable destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the movement toward the House is protected together with the inviolable place itself.
topics.reason: Adjectival agreement with the House constrains the sense; the tripled sanctity rows survive as structural payoff.

words.gloss_range: ongoing seeking of divine bounty and approval within a protected pilgrimage context
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, desiring, pursuing, and in other contexts overreaching; here the sacred objects make the seeking licit
words.prose: The verb {{ar:يَبْتَغُونَ}} ({{tr:yabtaghūna}}) supplies the protected pilgrims’ motive: they are seeking bounty and approval. The root can carry overreaching elsewhere, but this local clause and its objects narrow the pursuit into licensed pilgrimage seeking, with a close pilgrimage wording in 2:198.

topics.headline: licensed seeking defines pilgrim motive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pilgrims characterized by legitimate pursuit, not by hostile identity.
topics.reason: The hāl clause attaches to the pilgrims; object and context narrow the root’s ambivalence to legitimate seeking while preserving the boundary-sensitive payoff.

words.gloss_range: unspecified bounty or lawful gain sought from the Lord within pilgrimage
words.root_gloss_range: surplus, favor, excellence, bounty, and overflow; here it denotes sought provision or favor from God
words.prose: The indefinite object {{ar:فَضْلًۭا}} ({{tr:faḍlan}}) leaves the bounty open-ended. In this pilgrimage frame it can include lawful provision, but its source phrase makes the surplus a divine favor rather than a violation of sanctity, matching the pilgrimage permission language in 2:198.

topics.headline: open-ended divine bounty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that material gain can be framed as divine bounty rather than predatory acquisition.
topics.reason: The accusative object of seeking supports bounty; rows about trade and overflow are kept as narrowed by the source phrase and pilgrimage context.

words.gloss_range: source preposition locating bounty as coming from their Lord
words.prose: The preposition {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}) marks source. It turns the sought bounty toward the pilgrims’ Lord and away from any reading of gain through violating protected status.

topics.headline: source marked as the Lord
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pilgrims’ hoped-for gain sourced in God, not in exploiting sacred vulnerability.
topics.reason: QAC marks a source/governing preposition, and the rows emphasize origin and the pronoun shift toward the protected group.

words.gloss_range: possessed Lordship naming the pilgrims’ personal divine relation as source of bounty
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, nurturing, sustaining, mastering, and caring; here the possessed noun marks the pilgrims’ Lord as source and patron
words.prose: The phrase {{ar:رَّبِّهِمْ}} ({{tr:rabbihim}}) closes the bounty object with personal Lordship. It differs from the institutional divine-name frame by presenting the pilgrims’ journey as under their Lord’s care.

topics.headline: their Lord as patron of the pilgrims
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the protected outsiders are described through their own relation to God.
topics.reason: The genitive after the source preposition and possessive suffix support the personal relation; root-care pressure remains local.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle pairing material bounty with divine approval as sought objects
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pairs bounty with approval as co-objects of seeking. The clause holds worldly provision and divine acceptance together.

topics.headline: bounty paired with approval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that pilgrimage seeking is not reduced to commerce or detached spirituality.
topics.reason: QAC and CRITICAL rows agree that both accusative nouns are coordinated objects of the seeking verb.

words.gloss_range: open-ended divine good pleasure or approval sought alongside bounty
words.root_gloss_range: being pleased, accepting, approving, and contentment; here the noun denotes divine approval as a pilgrimage aim
words.prose: The noun {{ar:رِضْوَٰنًۭا}} ({{tr:riḍwānan}}) names approval as the second object of seeking. Its intensified nominal feel makes the goal larger than ordinary satisfaction, while the local pairing keeps it tied to the pilgrims’ devotional motive.

topics.headline: intensified divine approval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pilgrims’ aim includes God’s acceptance, not only gain.
topics.reason: The accusative conjoined object fixes the local function; pattern and approval rows are preserved as narrowed semantic force.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a new conditional section after the prohibition list
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens a new section rather than simply adding another protected item. After the prohibition cascade, the ayah turns to conditional permission.

topics.headline: major pivot to conditional permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah move from protected sanctities to a bounded release clause.
topics.reason: The rows identify a structural hinge, and QAC marks this conjunction as introducing the conditional release clause.

words.gloss_range: temporal conditional particle making the later permission depend on exiting sacred restriction
words.prose: The particle {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) makes the permission temporal and conditional. Hunting is only addressed after the state has changed, so the command form that follows is legally bounded and read from the consecration restriction already in view (5:1), not as a standing license.

topics.headline: permission depends on release condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hunting permission is conditional, not a standing license.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a temporal conditional, and the CRITICAL rows connect it to the answer particle and release from consecration.

words.gloss_range: completed exit from consecrated restriction before permission resumes
words.root_gloss_range: untying, release, lawful status, alighting, and dissolving; here Form I marks becoming released from restriction
words.prose: The verb {{ar:حَلَلْتُمْ}} ({{tr:ḥalaltum}}) is the release pivot. Unlike the earlier causative ban, this Form I wording marks the addressees as having become released from the sacred restriction before hunting is permitted.

topics.headline: becoming released, not making lawful
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a sharp difference between wrongful unbinding of sanctity and legitimate exit from restriction.
topics.reason: The same-root contrast with word 6 is supported by form difference and local conditional syntax; broader untying imagery is narrowed to state exit.

words.gloss_range: answer particle linking the permission to the prior release condition
words.prose: The particle {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) binds the result to the condition. It prevents the hunting imperative from being read apart from the prior release from restriction.

topics.headline: result tied to the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the permission grammatically fastened to the condition.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the answer/result particle, and all rows focus on the condition-result link.

words.gloss_range: permissioned hunting after release from consecrated restriction, not an obligation to hunt
words.root_gloss_range: hunting, catching, and game; here Form VIII imperative denotes deliberate hunting newly permitted by condition
words.prose: The imperative {{ar:ٱصْطَادُوا۟}} ({{tr:iṣṭādū}}) functions as permission after a ban, not as an obligation to hunt. Its distinctive Form VIII command gives the release clause legal weight: deliberate hunting is allowed only after the stated condition.

topics.headline: imperative of permission after restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command form restores permission rather than imposing a duty.
topics.reason: Attachment and legal rows support an imperative of permission; uniqueness and form rows are preserved as narrowed because they intensify the permissioned action.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the anti-retaliation warning after the release clause
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) immediately pivots from permitted hunting to prohibited retaliation. The ayah’s release clause is brief because ethical restraint must still fence the addressees.

topics.headline: pivot from permission to restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that lawful release does not open the door to hostility.
topics.reason: QAC marks a conjunction introducing the warning, and the rows identify the structural turn from permission to psychological restraint.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negation before an emphatic warning verb
words.prose: The particle {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) reasserts prohibition in the warning clause. It keeps hatred from becoming a permitted consequence of the previous release.

topics.headline: prohibition reasserted after permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears restraint return immediately after permission is granted.
topics.reason: QAC marks prohibitive negation, and the CRITICAL rows connect it to the energetic warning against transgression.

words.gloss_range: emphatic warning that hostile feeling must not impel the addressees into culpable action
words.root_gloss_range: crime, guilt, cutting off, earning culpability, and causing someone toward guilt; here it marks hatred as a forbidden driver
words.prose: The emphatic verb {{ar:يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:yajrimannakum}}) blocks hatred from driving the believers into guilt. The attached suffix makes the warning personal, and the heavy emphasis makes it more than advisory caution; a near-identical justice warning appears in 5:8.

topics.headline: hatred must not drive guilt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah regulates the emotional cause of retaliation, not only the outward act.
topics.reason: Energetic form, object suffix, and causal frame support the local reading; root guilt pressure is narrowed to incitement into culpable action.

words.gloss_range: intense hostility or animus functioning as the grammatical inciter of wrongdoing
words.root_gloss_range: hatred, aversion, and intense hostility; here the verbal noun names animus as the warning’s subject
words.prose: The noun {{ar:شَنَـَٔانُ}} ({{tr:shanaʾānu}}) makes hostility the grammatical driver in the warning. Its rare, agitated form gives the feeling momentum: this is not mild dislike but animus that must not be allowed to steer action.

topics.headline: agitated hatred as active cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees hatred treated as an active force that can move people toward overreach.
topics.reason: The nominative subject role and rare-intensity rows support the payoff; phonetic rows are folded into the same marked-hostility topic.

words.gloss_range: an indefinite group attached to hatred, socially embodied and tied to a past offense
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, establishing, and a people who stand together; here the noun denotes an identifiable group
words.prose: The noun {{ar:قَوْمٍ}} ({{tr:qawmin}}) attaches hatred to a group rather than an abstraction. Its standing-together root pressure makes the opposition socially embodied, while the following clause identifies a real offense without licensing retaliation.

topics.headline: group grievance without retaliation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even a real group grievance does not authorize collective overreaction.
topics.reason: Construct relation and following clause support group grievance; root posture is narrowed to social grouping.

words.gloss_range: complementizer introducing the cause or, by variant, possible condition of the barring grievance
words.prose: The particle {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) introduces the reason for the animus: the group barred the addressees. Variant evidence can extend the logic toward a possible case, but the local reading keeps the grievance factual in the warning frame.

topics.headline: reason clause for the grievance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the warning addresses a concrete grievance, not imaginary hostility.
topics.reason: QAC gives a complementizer after the hatred phrase; variant rows are narrowed to contrast without displacing the local factual clause.

words.gloss_range: past barring of the addressees from sacred access, with the injury encoded in the suffix
words.root_gloss_range: turning away, blocking, barring, and obstructing access; here it denotes actual prevention from the sacred site
words.prose: The verb {{ar:صَدُّوكُمْ}} ({{tr:ṣaddūkum}}) names the actual blocking suffered by the addressees. The warning is not built on pretending the grievance is false; it recognizes obstruction from sacred access and still refuses overreach, with related pilgrimage obstruction in 48:25.

topics.headline: real obstruction acknowledged
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah denies retaliation while still acknowledging a real injury.
topics.reason: Perfect verb plus object suffix support the historical injury; cross-reference rows are preserved with the concrete reference.

words.gloss_range: separation preposition marking the barred access vector
words.prose: The preposition {{ar:عَنِ}} ({{tr:ʿani}}) marks separation from the sacred place. It gives the grievance a spatial vector: the addressees were kept away from access.

topics.headline: exclusion from sacred place
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the harm as exclusion from a destination, not private dislike alone.
topics.reason: QAC marks a preposition after the barring verb, and the CRITICAL rows focus on blocked access.

words.gloss_range: the mosque as the definite sacred worship site from which access was blocked
words.root_gloss_range: prostrating, bowing low, submitting, and the place of prostration; here the noun denotes the sacred mosque site
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْمَسْجِدِ}} ({{tr:al-masjidi}}) identifies the barred destination as the worship site. Its place-noun formation from prostration makes the obstruction an exclusion from embodied submission, with the Hudaybiyya-related account in 48:25 providing the concrete memory.

topics.headline: barred worship space
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense targeted access to a place defined by submission.
topics.reason: The genitive prepositional object fixes the local site; root/place-noun rows survive as narrowed worship-space pressure.

words.gloss_range: inviolable modifier of the mosque within the obstruction clause
words.root_gloss_range: forbidding, consecrating, inviolability, and protected boundary/status; here it qualifies the mosque as sacred space
words.prose: The adjective {{ar:ٱلْحَرَامِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥarāmi}}) closes the obstruction phrase by marking the mosque as inviolable. This is the third sanctity marker in the ayah’s network of protected time, House, and mosque, but its position before the next result clause keeps grievance from becoming permission to overstep.

topics.headline: sacred-site grievance fenced from overreach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the grievance at a sacred site acknowledged, then fenced from retaliatory transgression.
topics.reason: Genitive adjectival agreement constrains the word to the mosque; structural rows about tripled sanctity and the next clause are preserved.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive/complement particle introducing the forbidden result of hatred
words.prose: The particle {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) introduces the outcome that hatred must not cause. It turns the warning from inner feeling to the legal result: transgression.

topics.headline: result clause names the danger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees emotion judged by the action it might produce.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle before the subjunctive verb, and the rows identify the cause-to-result frame.

words.gloss_range: forbidden overstepping or transgression as the result hatred must not cause
words.root_gloss_range: crossing, running beyond, hostility, aggression, and overstepping a boundary; here Form VIII selects ethical transgression
words.prose: The verb {{ar:تَعْتَدُوا۟}} ({{tr:taʿtadū}}) names the forbidden result as overstepping. The root’s motion-beyond-limit field makes retaliation feel like crossing a line, while the local form and warning frame select ethical transgression, a restraint also voiced in 5:87 and 2:190.

topics.headline: retaliation as boundary crossing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even provoked retaliation is named as crossing a boundary.
topics.reason: Subjunctive result syntax supports the local sense; root motion and formula rows are narrowed into boundary-crossing payoff with concrete references.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the positive cooperation command
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the positive command section. After forbidding retaliation, the ayah moves from specific pilgrimage restraint toward the universal ethical binary of cooperation in good versus cooperation in wrongdoing.

topics.headline: turn to constructive cooperation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move beyond non-retaliation into constructive social ethics.
topics.reason: The rows and QAC grammar identify a new syntactic unit introducing the positive reciprocal command.

words.gloss_range: plural reciprocal command to mutually assist within the approved ethical domain
words.root_gloss_range: help, assistance, support, and seeking aid; here Form VI selects horizontal mutual cooperation
words.prose: The command {{ar:تَعَاوَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:taʿāwanū}}) requires reciprocal help. The root’s aid field becomes horizontal in this Form VI pattern: the community is to build virtue together, and the same social mechanism will soon be morally filtered by its object.

topics.headline: reciprocal cooperation for good
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is mutual participation, not one-way charity or isolated virtue.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form VI imperative, and CRITICAL rows distinguish mutual cooperation from one-way aid while preserving the positive-negative pairing.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the basis or domain on which cooperation is to operate
words.prose: The preposition {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) makes cooperation rest upon a domain. Mutual aid is not open-ended; its moral status depends on the object that follows.

topics.headline: domain of cooperation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that cooperation is morally constrained by what it supports.
topics.reason: QAC marks the preposition governing the following nouns, and the rows emphasize domain or basis.

words.gloss_range: definite virtue, righteousness, or expansive goodness as the first cooperation domain
words.root_gloss_range: righteousness, goodness, truthfulness, dutifulness, and also open land/solid ground; here the moral virtue sense is selected
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْبِرِّ}} ({{tr:al-birri}}) names the first positive domain for cooperation. Local syntax selects moral virtue, while the root’s solid-ground pressure makes that virtue feel like stable social terrain; 2:177 supplies a fuller Qur’anic definition of this domain.

topics.headline: recognized virtue as firm ground
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that cooperation is grounded in a recognized ethical domain, not generic niceness.
topics.reason: The governed definite abstract noun selects moral virtue; land/root pressure is narrowed to image, and the 2:177 definition row is retained with reference.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle joining virtue and protective God-consciousness as one cooperation domain
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pairs virtue with protective God-consciousness. The positive pole is not one-dimensional: outward good and inward guarding form the shared basis of legitimate cooperation.

topics.headline: positive pair completed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees outward goodness and inward guarding fused rather than offered as alternatives.
topics.reason: QAC gives coordination of the two genitive domains; CRITICAL rows identify a paired positive unit.

words.gloss_range: protective God-conscious guarding as the second positive domain of cooperation
words.root_gloss_range: guarding, shielding, protecting, and taking precaution; here the abstract noun names the moral domain of protective piety
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ}} ({{tr:al-taqwā}}) turns protective God-consciousness into a domain for joint action. Its shielding field makes the positive command preventive as well as constructive, answering the opening protection of sacred signs with inner guarding.

topics.headline: protective piety as cooperation domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that cooperation aims at prevention and guarding, not only visible good deeds.
topics.reason: The governed abstract noun fixes local function; root shielding and opening-to-closing rows survive as narrowed payoff.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening the antithetical prohibition after the positive cooperation command
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) turns the positive command into its negative mirror. The ayah now tests cooperation by what it helps, not merely by the fact of helping.

topics.headline: hinge into the negative mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same social mechanism split by moral object.
topics.reason: The rows identify antithetical coordination and mirror structure; QAC marks a conjunction before the negative particle.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle negating reciprocal cooperation in the negative domain
words.prose: The {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) before the repeated cooperation verb forbids mutual aid when its object is corrupt. The same capacity for social support now receives a negative boundary.

topics.headline: ban on misdirected cooperation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears that collective capacity itself must pass a moral filter.
topics.reason: QAC marks prohibitive negation and the CRITICAL rows connect it to the negative mirror of cooperation.

words.gloss_range: negated reciprocal cooperation, forbidding social support networks for sin and aggression
words.root_gloss_range: help, support, assistance, and mutual aid; here Form VI is reused under negative scope
words.prose: The repeated verb {{ar:تَعَاوَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:taʿāwanū}}) shows that the social mechanism is the same as before, but its domain has changed. Mutual aid can amplify evil, so the ayah forbids enabling networks of sin and aggression.

topics.headline: reciprocal help can enable wrongdoing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that wrongdoing can be communal through enabling, not only through direct commission.
topics.reason: The repeated Form VI verb and matched prepositional frame support the mirror reading; variant and sound rows are folded into the same repeated-command payoff.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the basis on which forbidden cooperation would operate
words.prose: The preposition {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) repeats the domain frame. It makes the ethical binary exact: cooperation is judged by the ground it stands on.

topics.headline: negative domain frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the negative pair placed in the exact same syntactic slot as the positive pair.
topics.reason: QAC marks the second preposition governing the negative pair, and CRITICAL rows emphasize parallel domain syntax.

words.gloss_range: recognized domain of culpable sin or guilt as the first forbidden cooperation object
words.root_gloss_range: sin, guilt, moral burden, and slowing or impeding; here the definite abstract noun names culpable wrongdoing
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْإِثْمِ}} ({{tr:al-ithmi}}) names the first negative domain. Its burden and impediment pressure makes sin feel morally weighty, while the definite abstract form treats it as a recognized category of guilt in the fixed negative pair.

topics.headline: sin as culpable burden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the forbidden domain is weighty culpability, not a neutral mistake.
topics.reason: The governed definite abstract noun selects sin/guilt; root weight rows are narrowed to semantic pressure and paired-ethics rows are retained.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle joining sin and aggression as the prohibited cooperation domain
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pairs sin with aggression. Together they answer the positive pair and complete the four-term moral map of the cooperation command.

topics.headline: negative pair completed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees sin and aggression as distinct but joined poles of the forbidden social domain.
topics.reason: QAC gives coordination of the two negative genitives, and the CRITICAL rows identify the pair as the negative pole.

words.gloss_range: hostile boundary-violating aggression as the second forbidden cooperation domain
words.root_gloss_range: crossing, hostility, aggression, running beyond, and transgressing limits; here the noun names sustained overreach as a social domain
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿudwāni}}) closes the negative pair with aggression. It echoes the earlier forbidden overstepping in noun form, making boundary violation a social domain of cooperation to avoid; its intense overreach pressure also answers the agitated hatred named earlier, while structurally it stands opposite protective guarding.

topics.headline: aggression as systemic overreach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that personal overstepping becomes a collective domain that must not be supported.
topics.reason: The definite abstract noun selects aggression; root, pair, and verb-to-noun rows are narrowed into systemic overreach payoff.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening the sealing God-directed command and rationale
words.prose: The conjunction {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the closing command. After the cooperation binary, the ayah turns from communal behavior to direct accountability before God.

topics.headline: final transition to divine accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees horizontal social ethics gathered into vertical accountability.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a conjunction introducing the final command, and the rows emphasize the closing transition.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative to guard oneself in relation to God after the ethical sequence
words.root_gloss_range: guarding, shielding, protecting, and taking precaution; here Form VIII imperative commands active God-conscious self-guarding
words.prose: The imperative {{ar:ٱتَّقُوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqū}}) makes guarding an action. It reprises the earlier positive domain as a direct command: the addressees must actively guard themselves before God before the punishment rationale seals the ayah.

topics.headline: active self-guarding before God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole sequence is gathered into active protective accountability, not left as social policy alone.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form VIII imperative, and the CRITICAL rows connect the final command to the prior cooperation antithesis and accountability clause.

words.gloss_range: divine name as the direct object orienting the final guarding command
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field with stable proper-name reference here
words.prose: The divine name {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) completes the guarding command as its object. The same name then reappears in the rationale, binding obedience to the divine agent who enforces accountability.

topics.headline: God as object of the guarding command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final ethics directed toward God’s accountability, not abstract morality alone.
topics.reason: QAC marks the accusative object of the imperative; rows about repeated divine name and envelope are retained as structural payoff.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle introducing the closing reason clause
words.prose: The particle {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) introduces the reason for the final command with emphasis. The ayah’s closure is not merely advisory; it asserts the consequence frame as a sealing rationale that places the commands under divine sovereignty and punishment.

topics.headline: emphatic rationale for the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final warning as asserted rationale, not optional reflection.
topics.reason: QAC marks an emphatic particle introducing the closing clause, matching the CRITICAL rows on asserted rationale.

words.gloss_range: divine name as the subject under the emphatic particle in the punishment clause
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field with stable proper-name reference here
words.prose: The divine name {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) becomes the subject of the final warning. The legal and ethical body of the ayah is closed by direct theological accountability, linking the opening God-owned signs to God-governed punishment.

topics.headline: divine subject of the warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees punishment framed as God-governed accountability.
topics.reason: QAC marks the accusative subject under the emphatic particle, and the rows focus on God as the warning’s subject.

words.gloss_range: severe, forceful predicate bound to punishment in the closing formula
words.root_gloss_range: tightening, strengthening, severity, force, and hardness; here the adjective predicates severe force of punishment
words.prose: The adjective {{ar:شَدِيدُ}} ({{tr:shadīdu}}) predicates severity as a stable quality of the punishment clause. Its tightening and force field makes the warning hard-edged, and the same closing formula appears in pilgrimage context at 2:196.

topics.headline: severe consequence named as stable quality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closure specifies the force of consequence rather than giving a vague warning.
topics.reason: The predicate construction and construct relation support severity; formula rows are retained with concrete reference.

words.gloss_range: definite punishment or pursuing consequence completing the severity construct
words.root_gloss_range: following after, consequence, heel-following, punishment, and recompense; here the noun names punitive accountability
words.prose: The noun {{ar:ٱلْعِقَابِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿiqābi}}) completes the final construct with punishment as consequence. Its following-after root pressure makes accountability feel like what trails the act, while the definite noun seals the ayah with a known punitive category; the formula also appears in 2:196, 2:211, 3:11, and 5:98.

topics.headline: punishment as following consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that violation is closed by consequence that follows the act, not arbitrary force.
topics.reason: The genitive construct complement fixes the local punishment sense; root consequence and formula rows survive as narrowed payoff with concrete references.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired forms of ح ل ل at words 5 and 25 frame repeated ح ر م protections and the later permission to hunt.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah organizes conduct as state transitions: protected signs, times, places, offerings, and travelers may not be prematurely unbound, while release from the protected state opens a bounded activity. Permission is therefore timed and relational rather than a permanent property of the hunted thing.

activation_trace.role: The image of a restriction dissolving links the initial ban on making protected things licit with the later transition out of restriction.
Prohibition and prevention supply the protected states through which the release sequence moves.
Seeking and taking what resists names the newly available activity whose timing remains regulated.

changed_reading.before: The ayah lists sacred prohibitions and then separately permits hunting.
changed_reading.after: The prohibitions and hunting permission form one gated order in which legal capacity changes with state, time, and location.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: شعائر, الهدي, القلائد, آمين البيت, يبتغون, and رضوان describe marked beings moving toward a protected destination for an acknowledged purpose.
baseline_models.mechanism: Signs, offerings, collars, direction, destination, and seeking combine into a legibility system. Visible markers and declared orientation carry protection along a route, extending sanctity from a fixed house to vulnerable travelers and offerings in motion.

activation_trace.role: A sign that makes ritual status perceptible supplies the public legibility of the protected movement.
The offering sent toward the sanctuary supplies a protected object whose status travels with it.
A neck-worn marker makes the offering's protected claim externally recognizable.
Purposeful orientation supplies the travelers' directed movement rather than mere presence near a site.
The dwelling or refuge supplies the destination around which the protected corridor is organized.
Active seeking supplies the travelers' intelligible purpose on the route.
Sought abundant approval gives the journey a non-hostile declared end.

changed_reading.before: The ayah protects a collection of sacred objects and pilgrims.
changed_reading.after: The ayah creates a mobile safe-passage regime in which visible markers, orientation, and purpose extend protection from sanctuary to route.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joining يجرمنكم, شنآن, صدّوكم, تعتدوا, and the paired تعاونوا clauses blocks hatred from becoming transgression and redirects collective capacity.
baseline_models.mechanism: A remembered obstruction can generate hostile affect, hostile affect can drive boundary crossing, and cooperation can multiply either repair or harm. The ayah interrupts the first causal chain and routes shared agency toward expansive good and protective restraint rather than delayed good and aggression.

activation_trace.role: The image of acquiring or causing an outcome casts hatred as a possible producer of wrongful action.
Hatred and enmity supply the affective pressure that the prohibition refuses to treat as authorization.
Diversion and repulsion supply the remembered injury without determining the response.
Crossing a limit supplies the prohibited behavioral conversion of injury into retaliation.
Mutual assistance supplies a shared amplifier whose moral direction must be selected.
Expansive good and obedience supply the constructive channel for collective power.
A barrier against harm supplies the self-limiting protection that governs both cooperation and retaliation.
Delay from good identifies the disabling channel into which cooperation must not be routed.

changed_reading.before: The ayah commands fairness toward enemies and recommends helping in good deeds.
changed_reading.after: The ayah is an affect-to-action firewall: it prevents injury from authorizing retaliation and treats cooperation as an amplifier that must be deliberately routed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding demand to complete binding agreements turns the focus ayah's repeated prohibitions into covenant maintenance. The collar is not only a ritual ornament: together with the knot and obligation images, it is a visible bearer of a social claim that others must honor rather than unbind.

activation_trace.role: Untying a knot supplies the focus prohibition's image of dissolving an established protection.
Placing an obligation on the neck supplies the marked offering as a carrier of binding responsibility.
Completion without deficiency makes protection of the focus ayah's marked parties an act of fulfilling rather than merely observing.
A firmly concluded covenant supplies the binding social relation that the visible marker externalizes.

structural_cues: 5:1 places fulfillment of agreements immediately before 5:2 and shares the ح ل ل state vocabulary.
The focus sequence moves from ritual signs to collars and directed travelers before it addresses retaliation and cooperation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies completion, binding agreements, untying, and a neck-borne obligation; I infer that visible ritual status externalizes a covenant others owe to the marked bearer. A live alternative is that 5:1 governs contracts generally while 5:2 begins an unrelated ritual list.

changed_reading.before: Visible sacred markers identify things that must not be disturbed.
changed_reading.after: Visible sacred markers carry enforceable relational claims, so disturbing the marked traveler or offering amounts to unbinding a covenant of protection.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later hunting rule fills out what happens after release: predatory capacity is trained, delegated, made to hold for another, and accompanied by articulated remembrance. Leaving a restricted state opens acquisition, but lawful agency remains disciplined at the point of capture.

activation_trace.role: Dissolution of restriction supplies the transition after which hunting becomes available.
Seeking and taking resistant prey supplies the released activity whose execution needs specification.
Knowledge made available through repeated teaching turns raw predatory force into instructed agency.
Hunting animals supply delegated capture rather than an unstructured human taking.
Holding and retaining supplies control at the decisive boundary between pursuit and usable acquisition.
Running the name on the tongue makes the capture explicitly accountable rather than merely successful.

structural_cues: 5:4 repeats ح ل ل twice and answers a question about what is permitted after 5:2's release-and-hunt transition.
Teaching occurs three times around the hunting animals, followed by holding, naming, protective restraint, and accounting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies release, trained hunting agents, retained prey, and spoken remembrance; I infer that the later ayah operationalizes the focus permission as controlled delegated capture. A live alternative is that 5:4 regulates food separately and does not qualify the force of 5:2's hunting license.

changed_reading.before: Once the protected state ends, hunting is simply permitted.
changed_reading.after: Release restores activity but not unbounded predation: acquisition remains trained, controlled, attributable, and answerable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The near-verbatim return of hatred as a possible producer of wrongdoing moves the focus rule from physical trespass into testimony and judgment. The added scale, balance, repeated justice command, and proximity to protective restraint make hostile affect a test of calibration across action and adjudication.

activation_trace.role: Acquiring or producing an outcome supplies the causal hinge by which hatred could generate transgression.
Hatred supplies the pressure that must not set the response standard.
Boundary crossing supplies the focus ayah's first named failure mode under hostile affect.

A straight balance supplies a public standard that hostile feeling may not tilt.
The repeated causal hinge explicitly transfers the focus warning into the justice setting.
The repeated hatred term identifies the same affective input across both settings.
Justice in judgment and conduct supplies the positively repeated response to hatred.
Nearness supplies an explicit relation between calibrated justice and protective restraint.
Repeated self-protection closes the justice instruction as a discipline against affective distortion.

structural_cues: 5:8 repeats the rare يجرمنكم شنآن construction from 5:2 before replacing transgression with failure to act justly.
The sequence in 5:8 moves from public witness and balance to a doubled justice command and then to nearness to protective restraint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical repetition plus testimony, balance, justice, and nearness; I infer that 5:8 is an operational expansion of 5:2 from bodily or spatial retaliation to evidentiary and judicial calibration. A live alternative is that the two ayat are parallel exhortations without one specifying the other.

changed_reading.before: Do not answer exclusion from the sanctuary with aggressive retaliation.
changed_reading.after: The same anti-retaliation discipline governs evidence and judgment: hatred must alter neither another's access nor the measure used to assess them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The paired covenant accounts show hostility becoming durable when binding commitments are broken or neglected. One sequence answers breach with pardon and gracious turning aside; the next depicts forgotten obligation followed by induced enmity and hatred. The focus ayah's cooperation rule therefore controls whether collective memory interrupts injury or institutionalizes it.

activation_trace.role: Hatred and enmity supply the focus affect whose persistence the later covenant sequences explain.
Mutual assistance supplies the collective mechanism that can stabilize either repair or wrongdoing.
Undoing what was firmly built supplies the initiating covenant failure.
Leaving punishment and effacing fault supplies one non-recursive response to repeated breach.
Graciously turning aside from fault supplies a second way not to transmit breach into retaliation.
Neglecting and leaving aside a remembered share supplies the loss of a coordinating obligation.
Incitement supplies the directional move by which neglected obligation becomes active intergroup hostility.
Enmity supplies the social relation that hardens after covenantal forgetting.
Affective aversion supplies the internal counterpart to the external relation of enmity.

structural_cues: 5:13 and 5:14 are adjacent covenant-failure sequences that both include forgetting but display different response paths.
The focus ayah places positive and negative cooperation immediately after refusing hatred-driven transgression.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covenant undoing, forgetting, pardon, gracious turning aside, incitement, enmity, and hatred; I infer a causal contrast between interrupting and reproducing covenantal injury. A live alternative is that the two later sequences only report distinct communal histories and do not model the focus cooperation commands.

changed_reading.before: The focus ayah restrains an immediate retaliatory impulse caused by a past obstruction.
changed_reading.after: The focus ayah also governs the long social afterlife of injury: shared practices can either metabolize breach through restraint or preserve it as organized enmity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing movement sequence places sacred land, turning back, a gate, trust, refusal to act, renewed prohibition, and wandering around a contested threshold. This expands the focus protection of sanctuary-bound travelers into a reciprocal passage ethic: sacredness forbids hostile obstruction but also demands coordinated, non-paralyzed movement through a rightful entrance.

activation_trace.role: Purposeful orientation supplies the sanctuary-bound movement whose passage the focus ayah protects.
A dwelling or refuge supplies the protected destination.
Diversion and repulsion supply the wrongful denial of access that must not be mirrored.
A protected spatial precinct supplies the boundary whose meaning is tested by movement toward it.
Mutual assistance supplies the coordinated capacity needed to preserve or traverse the passage.
A purified place supplies a second sacred destination approached through commanded movement.
Returning or being turned back supplies the reversal that aborts directed access.
Turning one's back supplies embodied withdrawal from the commanded route.
An entrance supplies the specific threshold through which coordinated passage must occur.
Reliance supplies courage for action without making aggressive force the sole ground of entry.
Sitting out action supplies the collective paralysis opposed to directed passage.
Renewed prohibition supplies the consequence by which refused entry becomes prolonged exclusion.

structural_cues: 5:21 commands entry into sacred land and forbids turning back; 5:23 narrows action to entering a gate with trust.
5:24 answers with explicit refusal and sitting, while 5:26 pairs renewed prohibition with the branchless ت ي ه occurrence for wandering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two sacred destinations, obstruction or reversal, a gate, coordinated counsel, refusal, sitting, prohibition, and wandering; I infer a reciprocal passage ethic in which sanctuary is protected by both non-obstruction and responsible movement. A live alternative is that the closing narrative concerns a distinct military entry and should not be mapped onto pilgrimage access.

changed_reading.before: The focus ayah protects people already traveling toward a sacred destination and forbids revenge for prior exclusion.
changed_reading.after: The focus ayah regulates a whole threshold system: do not block protected approach, do not turn sacred access into retaliation, and organize shared agency so fear does not collapse directed movement into exclusion or stasis.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the disease-transfer branch of ع د و is distant from the juridical sense of aggression. It remains anchored because ع د و occurs twice beside reciprocal cooperation in 5:2 and returns as social enmity after incitement in 5:14. Downstream prose should present transmission only as a network analogy for reproduced hostility, not as the lexical gloss of عدوان or as a medical claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two تعاونوا clauses make conduct transmissible through a group, while the split branch inventory for focus-root ع د و includes transfer of disease alongside aggression and enmity.

activation_trace.role: Mutual assistance supplies the contact network through which a disposition can be multiplied.
Transfer of disease supplies the deliberately branch-distant image of aggression propagating through social contact.
Hatred and enmity supply the affective load that the analogy treats as reproducible.
Incitement supplies an active mechanism that sets hostility moving between parties.
The same transfer image recasts enduring intergroup enmity as a propagated relation while remaining explicitly analogical.
Affective aversion supplies what is carried internally as enmity spreads socially.

changed_reading.before: Do not collaborate in sinful or aggressive acts.
changed_reading.after: Do not let cooperative networks become vectors through which injured hostility is transmitted, stabilized, and reproduced as new boundary crossing.

strongest_changes: The repeated 5:2 and 5:8 hatred construction turns anti-retaliation into a single standard governing access, testimony, and judgment.
5:1 makes marked ritual protection covenantal: the visible sign carries a binding claim that others must fulfill.
5:4 shows that release from restriction restores agency without removing training, control, naming, or accountability.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah became a threshold-and-network protocol rather than a flat rule list: it marks mobile claims, gates changing permissions, blocks hostile affect from setting standards, and directs collective power across sacred passage.
remaining_uncertainties: The covenant reading may overconnect 5:1's general agreements with the collars and ritual signs of 5:2.
The closing sacred-land narrative may illuminate passage structurally without directly specifying sanctuary access in 5:2.
The transmission outlier depends on a branch-distant image and must remain an explicit analogy.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Visible signs make an unseen perimeter.** `ش ع ر B006` supplies marking sign/ritual emblem, `ق ل د B002` the neck-garland, and `ح ر م B003` protected bounds. The listed month, offerings, collars, travelers, house, and mosque distribute visible markers across time, animal, person, and place. I infer that recognizing the signs causes restraint; the sacred perimeter is socially perceived before it is physically enforced.
2. **Hatred must not harvest a new offense.** `ج ر م B001` is cutting/harvesting and `ج ر م B003` earning or causing liability; `ش ن ء B001` supplies enmity. The packet gives prior obstruction and a prohibition on overstepping; I infer the causal arrow whereby cultivated hatred ripens into earned guilt. “Do not let hatred incriminate you” becomes an agrarian-causal warning about what resentment produces.
3. **Cooperation as seasoned collective strength.** `ع و ن B001` is help and backing, while its accepted `B003` image is seasoned repeated war. Coupled with `ب ر ر B005` (open dry land) and `و ق ي B001` (protective barrier), the repeated cooperate/do-not-cooperate construction evokes coordinated movement across exposed terrain. Exploratorily, I infer that righteousness and caution convert battle-tested collective capacity from aggression into mutual protection.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Visible collars carry invisible obligations.** Fixed **ق ل د / B004** (“placing an obligation around someone’s neck”) lets the sacrificial *qalāʾid* function simultaneously as material garlands and public burdens of protection. The ayah moves from marked offerings and pilgrims to cooperative duties, and 5:7 names the covenant explicitly. I infer that a visible neck-marker makes others answerable for how they treat its bearer. The prohibition on violation thus reads as recognition of an externally legible covenant, not merely respect for an object.
2. **Hatred must not harvest an offense.** Fixed **ج ر م / B003** (“earning and causing to incur”) makes *lā yajrimannakum* causal: hostility can make a group incur transgression. The ayah itself reverses obstruction into a command not to overstep and then redirects collective energy into **ع و ن / B001** (“helping and backing”). I supply the arrow that affect recruits action unless cooperation reroutes it. The reading changes from “remain fair despite dislike” to a mechanism for preventing grievance from producing a new liability.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:7’s explicit *mīthāq* made the collars newly legible as public covenant markers rather than sacrificial decoration alone.

baseline.text: Ey inananlar! Allah'ın işaretlerine, haram aya, kurbanlık hayvanlara, boyunlarına işaret takılanlara ve Rablerinden lütuf ve hoşnutluk arayarak Kutsal Ev'e yönelenlere saygısızlık etmeyin. İhramdan çıktığınızda avlanabilirsiniz. Sizi Mescid-i Haram'dan alıkoydukları için bir topluluğa duyduğunuz kin sizi saldırganlığa itmesin. İyilik ve Allah'a karşı gelmekten sakınma konusunda yardımlaşın; günah ve saldırganlıkta yardımlaşmayın. Allah'a karşı gelmekten sakının. Şüphesiz Allah'ın cezası ağırdır.

findings.text: Ay, kurbanlık, gerdanlık, ziyaretçi, ev ve mescit üzerindeki görünür işaretler, kutsal sınırı fiziksel zorlamadan önce toplumsal olarak algılanır kılar.
Beslenen nefret, yeni bir haksızlığı doğurup işleyeni de onun sorumluluğu altına sokabilir.
İyilik ve sakınma uğrundaki yardımlaşma, sınanmış toplu gücü saldırıdan karşılıklı korunmaya yöneltir.
Kurbanlığın boynundaki görünür gerdanlık, onu görenleri taşıyıcısına karşı koruyucu bir yükümlülük altına sokar.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A binding structure governs conduct until it is faithfully completed or explicitly loosened.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The same latent mechanics connect covenantal obligation, a tightened knot, and the controlled loosening of a prohibition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Lawful Release Without Rupture
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A restriction is deliberately loosened so that a previously bounded thing may pass into lawful use.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: untying a knot `quranic:root_000351:B001/m01`; lifting a prohibition `quranic:root_000351:B003/m01`; protected or inviolable boundary `quranic:root_000313:B006/m01`; covenantal bond `quranic:root_001623:B004/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Lawfulness is not depicted as the absence of structure but as authorized release from it. The covenant remains intact while particular restrictions are opened.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A protected status becomes legible by being physically marked or held close to the body.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sanctuary observance is reframed through the concrete technologies of collars, cords, and bodily restraint.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Marked Offering
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A cord is twisted and placed as a visible neck-marker, making protected destination and status publicly recognizable.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: twisting a cord `quranic:root_001249:B001/m01`; sacrificial neck-marker `quranic:root_001249:B002/m01`; tight necklace or collar `quranic:root_000444:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The offering’s protected status is carried on its body. A twisted collar externalizes an invisible legal claim and warns observers against interference.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Just judgment restrains forces that would otherwise bend testimony or extend violence.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Judicial impartiality and physical protection share one latent operation: stopping a force before it reaches its target.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Withheld Hand
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Hatred generates intended aggression, but the reaching hand is intercepted and prevented from completing it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hatred `quranic:root_000820:B001/m01`; culpable causing or earning `quranic:root_000239:B003/m01`; transgression `quranic:root_000993:B001/m01`; extending the hand `quranic:root_000116:B004/m01`; restraining or preventing `quranic:root_001308:B002/m01`; hand as instrument `quranic:root_001693:B001/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The remembered protection gives bodily form to the judicial command. The same ethics that stops hatred from moving a verdict also stops a hostile hand from arriving as violence.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الأمن ضد الخوف، والأمان وإعطاء الأمنة، والأمانة ضد الخيانة وما اؤتمن عليه، والآمن والمأمن والاستئمان، والأمين والمأمون وما يوثق به، ومنه وثاقة الناقة الأمون.
يدخل فيه الإيمان بمعنى التصديق، وتصديق الخبر أو الوعد، والإيمان على سبيل الشريعة أو إذعان النفس للحق حيث نصت المصادر، واستعمال مؤمن بمعنى مصدق الوعد.
يدخل فيه آمين في الدعاء بالمد والقصر، والتأمين بمعنى قول آمين، وتفسيرها باستجب أو اللهم افعل أو كذلك فليكن، مع ذكر قول من جعلها اسما من أسماء الله.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bağlı bir düğümün açılmasını ve bunun sonucunda bağın çözülmesini doğrudan anlatır. Bu nedenle dalın kimliği, daha genel serbest bırakma ya da yasak kaldırma anlamlarına genişletilmeden korunabilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalnızca düğümün açılmasını bildiren kuruluşla sınırlıdır ve yalın köke genel bir çözme anlamı yüklemez.

concept_map.definition: Sıkılmış ya da bağlanmış bir düğümü açarak bağın çözülmesini sağlama eylemidir.

facets.statement: Bağlı düğüm açılır ve düğümü oluşturan sıkılık ortadan kalkar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, düğümü açma işlemi ile düğümün çözülmesi sonucunu birlikte temel anlam sayar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bağlanmış bir düğümün açılıp sıkılığının giderildiği bütün bağlamlarda kullanılır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir metinde bağlı düğümün fiilen açılması anlatıldığında doğal bir yüklem olarak kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yasaklanmış olmanın karşıtını, kutsal veya sözleşmesel kısıttan çıkmayı ve bir şeyi izinli kılmayı aynı kısıtın kalkması çekirdeğinde birleştirir. Bu çekirdek, salt yerleşme veya borcun zorunlu hale gelmesinden ayrıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın durum bildiren biçimler ile bir şeyi izinli sayma veya kılma kuruluşları ayrı yüzler olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi, yer ya da şey üzerindeki yasağın veya bağlayıcı dokunulmazlığın kalkması ve böylece ona izin verilmiş olmasıdır. Eylemli kuruluşlarda bir şeyi izinli kılma ya da izinli sayma da bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Yasak veya bağlayıcı kısıt kalkar ve ilgili kişi ya da şey izinli duruma geçer.
Kısıttan çıkma, kutsal bölge, törensel durum veya koruma anlaşması gibi belirli sınırlara uygulanabilir.
Bir şeyi izinli kılma veya izinli sayma, durum değişikliğinin ettirgen ve yargısal uzantılarıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yasağın karşıtı olan izinli durumu, kısıttan çıkmayı ve izin verme eylemini ortak bir çözülme ilişkisiyle açıklar.

concept_gloss.text: yasağın kalkması ve izinli duruma gelme

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi topluluğun savaşta kullandığı tanıtıcı çağrıyı, kutsal ziyaretin belirti ve uygulamalarını, tören yerini, adanmış hayvanı kanatarak tanınır kılmayı ve bir insanı yaralayıp kanatmayı birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve belirti ve kanla belirleme bağını doğru yansıtır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Karışık ve yalın olmayan kapsam, genel belirti alanını savaş çağrısı, kutsal tören ve kanatarak işaretleme kalıplarından ayırmayı gerektirir; özel uygulamalar genel anlama yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir topluluğu ya da adanmış varlığı tanınır kılan belirti veya ortak çağrı dalın çekirdeğidir. Savaşta ayırt edici çağrı, kutsal ziyaretin belirti, uygulama ve yerleri, adanmış hayvanı kanatarak belirleme ve bir insanı saplayarak kanatma bunun özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir topluluğun üyelerinin birbirini tanımasını sağlayan ortak savaş çağrısı veya belirti temel anlamdır.
Kutsal ziyaretin tanıtıcı belirtileri, uygulamaları, adanmış hayvanı ve belirlenmiş tören yeri bu çekirdeğin dinsel özelleşmesidir.
Adanmış hayvanın hörgücünü yaralayıp kan akıtarak onun adanmış olduğunu görünür kılma, eylemli bir belirleme biçimidir.
Bir insanı mızrak ya da benzeri araçla saplayıp kanatmak, belirleme amacından ayrılmış kanatma uzantısıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak kaynak anlatısı savaşta tanınmayı sağlayan çağrı veya belirtiyi, kutsal ziyaretin göstergelerini ve uygulamalarını, tören yerini ve adanmış hayvanı kanatarak belirleme işlemini bir araya getirir; insanı saplayarak kanatma da eylemin genişlemiş kullanımıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ana bölümü, yapılmasına veya çiğnenmesine izin verilmeyen şeyi açıkça karşıt kutbuyla tanımlar. Aynı kanıt içindeki yıkılmış yerleşim kalıbı ise olanaksızlık, kesin hüküm veya geri dönmeme zorunluluğu biçiminde yorumlandığından genel yasak anlamına doğrudan katılmamalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın yasak anlamını temel alır; sabit yerleşim kalıbındaki özel yorumları bağımlı bir kaynak çeşidi olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir eylemin, nesnenin veya hakkın yapılmasına, kullanılmasına ya da çiğnenmesine izin verilmemesidir. Yıkılmış bir yerleşimin geri dönmesiyle ilgili sabit kalıpta ise anlam, olanaksızlık ile kesin bir geri dönmeme hükmü arasında yorumlanır.

facets.statement: Temel anlam, izin verilenin karşıtı olarak hükmen veya kural gereği yasaklanmış şeydir.
Yıkılmış bir yerleşim hakkındaki sabit kullanım, geri dönüşün olanaksızlığı veya geri dönmemenin kesinliği biçiminde açıklanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar genel olarak izin verilmeyen ve dokunulması caiz görülmeyen şeyi bildirir; sabit yerleşim ifadesinin nasıl anlaşılacağı konusunda ise birden çok açıklama aktarır.

concept_gloss.text: yapılması veya çiğnenmesi yasak olan şey
concept_gloss.applicability: Yalın çekirdekte, izin verilmeyen eylem, nesne veya hak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yasaklama ile izin verilmeme çekirdeğini birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem dinsel bakımdan dokunulmaz iki şehir ve çevresini hem de kuyu, ev, ırmak ve ibadethane gibi yerlere bağlı hak ve kullanım çevresini kapsar. Bunların ortak yanı korunan mekânsal çevredir; ancak kutsallık yalnızca ilk gruba aittir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın kapsam, korunan yer ve çevresi üzerinden tanımlanır; kutsallık bütün mekânsal kullanımlara genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir yerin dokunulmaz veya korunmuş sayılan kendisi ile ona bağlı çevredir. Bu çevre kutsal bir bölge olabileceği gibi kuyu, ev, ırmak ya da ibadethanenin hak ve hizmet alanı da olabilir.

facets.statement: Kutsal sayılan şehir veya bölge, sınırları ve yakın çevresiyle birlikte korunmuş mekândır.
Kuyu, ev, ırmak veya ibadethane çevresindeki kullanım hakları ve eklentiler de korunan mekânsal çevreyi oluşturur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar kutsal şehirlerin ve çevrelerinin dokunulmazlığını, ayrıca yapı ve su kaynaklarının çevresindeki hak ve hizmet alanlarını ortak bir korunan çevre kavramında birleştirir.

error_profile.preserves: Korunan mekânı ve ona bağlı çevresel hakları birlikte korur.
